quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive in an area.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are dangerous, like wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: What lights should you use when weather or darkness requires headlights?

options.text: Parking lights
High beams
Low beams

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror
Look in your side mirror
Turn and look over your shoulders

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn and look over your shoulders
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must turn your head and look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: A person carrying a white cane or walking with a guide dog is most likely:

options.text: Deaf
Part of a traffic study
Blind
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind person. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear
Leave more space between your vehicle and the car ahead
Drive carefully near other vehicles
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between you and other vehicles because slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations
Keeps traffic moving safely
Keeps other drivers alert

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head
Can see directly behind your vehicle
Can see in your rearview mirror
Can see in your side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic signal or stop sign, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed
Stop, look both ways, then proceed
Yield to all other drivers
Be ready to yield if needed

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed
questions.explanation: At uncontrolled intersections, be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. Slow down, cover your brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
Time between drinks
All three

questions.correctAnswerText: All three
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from too much drinking.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet directly behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beam when you are following closely behind another vehicle.

questions.question: When following which vehicle should you leave extra space in front?

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes or the rider falls. Also, motorcycles have only one tail light, making them hard to see at night.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if it is a divided highway.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights. Drive to the right edge and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your lane until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Help drivers behind you stay safe by driving at a steady speed and signaling turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because of low visibility. You cannot judge distance and other vehicles' speeds as well. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering the interstate from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Honk your horn so they know you are there.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes to give them room to merge safely, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to give them room to merge safely, if possible.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the interstate. Change lanes when possible to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep downgrade or hill is ahead.
Road construction area.
The road will narrow ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downgrade or hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers about a dangerous downgrade or hill ahead. The hill may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs?

options.text: Black letters on a white background
Black letters on a yellow background
White letters on a blue background
White letters on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs use yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs use orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or school crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns that the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or adjust your position.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road by turning the steering wheel slightly. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before steering back.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space as cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind them. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic speed.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Before merging, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: After an accident with an injured person, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured exactly where they are.
Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them without training can make small injuries worse. Keep them warm and give first aid. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop the flow.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to vehicles entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Stop inside the traffic circle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that moves counterclockwise around a center island and has no traffic signal. When entering, yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to situations ahead. This sign tells you a side road will cross ahead.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road curves ahead. Slow down.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions.
All carpool lanes from regular lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not cross. A broken yellow line means you may cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If you park your car in an unusual spot:

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car should not be a hazard. Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Drive a bit faster.
Be ready for anything.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-lane, two-way street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic.
Your car has the speed to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires clear visibility, space to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a car fast enough to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, watch the right side of the road ahead. Do not look at the headlights because the glare can blind you temporarily.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs show traffic rules you must obey. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign say?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped yellow signs mark no passing zones.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces alcohol's effect on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and make driving unsafe. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes crashes much more likely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going forward.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: When you are on a hill or curve.
When there is a solid line next to your lane.
When there is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
When your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive onto the shoulder to pass. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when another driver wants to pass. This gives them space in front of your car to complete their pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. These are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse them. Yield to them and drive safely when it is clear.

questions.question: Who must drivers obey?

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must follow instructions from flaggers at construction sites. They direct traffic to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign warns you of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: A car coming toward you has high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead of your vehicle:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. When you watch the road ahead and prepare to stop or change lanes, you drive more safely, use less fuel, and help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: If you become too drowsy to drive safely, you should:

options.text: Drink a large energy drink.
Exit the road and rest.
Open all the windows and turn on the air conditioning.
Talk to a friend on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and rest.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot drive safely. Your reactions are slower and your decision-making is reduced. If you feel drowsy while driving, leave the road and rest.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts you and the rider at risk. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid them. The risk of falling is higher on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If you find a vehicle defect that could affect safe driving, you should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving right away. Correct defects before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: On a freeway, look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot potential hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: Yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. Also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If you must drive in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect off fog and shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility.
